edits.match: USPSTF 2025 issues an I-statement for men; AACE, BHOF, and Endocrine Society support screening men
edits.new: **Men.** USPSTF 2025 issues an I-statement for men; AACE and BHOF support screening men ≥70 (and ≥50 with risk factors). The Endocrine Society 2012 men's guideline was retired Oct 2025 without replacement and is no longer an operative source.

edits.match: Serum calcium (corrected) — prior to each IV zoledronate or denosumab dose
edits.new: **Serum calcium (corrected)** — prior to each IV zoledronate or denosumab dose; before initiating any antiresorptive. Avoid hypocalcemia, especially with CKD. Denosumab (FDA Boxed Warning 2024): assess eGFR before prescribing; if eGFR <30 / dialysis, evaluate for CKD-MBD (nephrology input), correct Ca and replete Ca + activated vit D before dosing, and monitor serum Ca closely after each dose (peak risk weeks 2–5, range 2–10).

Baseline secondary-causes workup (Ca, 25-OH vit D, PTH, alk phos, Cr / eGFR, P, Mg, TSH, CBC, 24-hr urine Ca; SPEP / celiac / testosterone if indicated); CTX or P1NP bone-turnover markers (baseline + 3–6 mo after starting / changing therapy, and during drug holiday); eGFR before denosumab — if eGFR <30 / dialysis, CKD-MBD evaluation and close post-dose Ca monitoring (weeks 2–10; FDA Boxed Warning)

edits.match: ACP 2023 and BHOF 2022 recommend against routine BMD monitoring
edits.new: ACP 2023 (reaffirmed 2025) and BHOF 2022 recommend against routine BMD monitoring

edits.match: ACP does not recommend routine use
edits.new: ACP (2023; reaffirmed 2025) does not recommend routine use
**AACE update pending.** AACE lists its 2020 postmenopausal osteoporosis guideline as under revision (update in development as of Nov 2026); re-audit DXA-on-therapy intervals on publication.

edits.match: FRAX 10-year fracture risk recalculation — at baseline and as indicated when risk factors change
edits.new: **FRAX 10-year fracture risk recalculation** — at baseline and as indicated when risk factors change; at drug-holiday decision points. Major osteoporotic ≥20% or hip ≥3% triggers treatment. USPSTF 2025: in postmenopausal women <65 with risk factors, use a validated tool (FRAX, OST, ORAI, SCORE) to select for DXA; FRAX has no USPSTF screening threshold; race-specific FRAX calculators may underestimate risk in Asian, Black, and Hispanic patients.

edits.match: On active surveillance, NCCN v1.2025 and AUA/ASTRO 2022 endorse PSA every 6 months (often q3–6 mo in the first year), annual DRE, multiparametric MRI roughly every 1–3 years, and a confirmatory biopsy within 6–12 months of diagnosis followed by surveillance biopsies every 2–5 years or when triggered by PSA kinetics, new DRE findings, or rising PI-RADS
edits.new: On active surveillance, NCCN v5.2026 uses PSA every 3–6 months while AUA/ASTRO (2022; amended 2026) advises PSA generally no more often than every 6 months (conflict flagged; NCCN cadence retained); annual DRE (AUA allows every 1–2 years); MRI if the diagnostic biopsy was not MRI-guided and roughly every 1–3 years thereafter; a confirmatory biopsy within ~12 months (promptly for PI-RADS 4–5), then surveillance biopsies every 1–4 years or when triggered by PSA rise, new DRE findings, or rising PI-RADS — MRI does not replace periodic biopsy

edits.match: After curative therapy, PSA is checked every 6–12 months for 5 years and then annually
edits.new: After curative therapy, PSA is checked every 3–6 months for the first 2 years, every 6 months in years 2–5, and then annually (AUA/ASTRO 2026; more frequent than the NCCN / ACS 6–12-month schedule and adopted as the conservative interval)

edits.match: PSMA PET is now first-line at biochemical recurrence when conventional imaging is negative
edits.new: PSMA PET is preferred at PSA recurrence after exhaustion of local therapy (AUA/SUO 2026) and is an equal alternative to bone scan + cross-sectional imaging for staging unfavorable intermediate / high-risk disease (AUA/ASTRO 2026)

edits.match: DEXA at baseline and every 1–2 years with FRAX-guided bisphosphonate or denosumab use
edits.new: DEXA + FRAX at baseline, repeated 1 year after starting ADT and every 1–2 years thereafter, with FRAX-guided bisphosphonate or denosumab use

edits.match: PSA on active surveillance — every 3–6 months. Rising PSA or PSA density
edits.new: **PSA on active surveillance** — every 3–6 months (NCCN). AUA/ASTRO 2026 advises PSA generally no more often than every 6 months; interval may be individualized (less intense with low progression risk / limited life expectancy). Rising PSA: repeat PSA first, then MRI ± biopsy. PSA density >0.15 ng/mL/cc triggers re-evaluation.

edits.match: PSA post-radical prostatectomy — every 6–12 months for 5 years
edits.new: **PSA post-radical prostatectomy** — every 3–6 months for the first 2 years, every 6 months years 2–5, then annually (AUA/ASTRO 2026; NCCN / ACS allow 6–12 months × 5 yr). Target undetectable (<0.1 ng/mL; ultrasensitive <0.01); BCR = 2 consecutive PSA ≥0.2 ng/mL. Beyond 10 yr with undetectable PSA, duration is a shared decision.

edits.match: PSA post-radiation — every 6–12 months for 5 years, then annually
edits.new: **PSA post-radiation** — every 3–6 months for the first 2 years, every 6 months years 2–5, then annually (AUA/ASTRO 2026; NCCN / ACS allow 6–12 months × 5 yr). BCR = PSA nadir + 2 ng/mL (Phoenix).

edits.match: Abiraterone monitoring (LFTs, potassium, BP) — every 2 weeks
edits.new: **Abiraterone monitoring (LFTs, potassium, BP)** — every 2 weeks × first 3 months, then monthly. Also applies to high-risk localized / cN1 disease treated with RT + ADT + abiraterone / prednisone for 24 months (AUA/ASTRO 2026).

edits.match: eGFR / creatinine — per agent
edits.new: **Germline genetic testing** — offer to all patients with advanced prostate cancer; add somatic tumor testing in metastatic disease (PARP inhibitor eligibility; cascade testing of relatives).

edits.match: Confirmatory / surveillance prostate biopsy — within 6–12 months of AS enrollment
edits.new: **Confirmatory / surveillance prostate biopsy** — MRI first if diagnostic biopsy was not MRI-guided; PI-RADS 4–5 → prompt targeted confirmatory biopsy; PI-RADS 1–3 → confirmatory biopsy within ~12 months. Then every 1–4 years (age, health, progression risk, preference) or as triggered. MRI does not replace periodic biopsy. No upgrading to Grade Group ≥2 (high-volume) or ≥3.

edits.match: DEXA / BMD on ADT — baseline before ADT; every 1–2 years on ADT
edits.new: **DEXA / BMD on ADT** — baseline DXA + FRAX before / at ADT start; re-assess FRAX + DXA 1 year after starting ADT / systemic therapy (greatest loss in year 1), then every 1–2 years per risk. FRAX 10-yr hip ≥3% or major osteoporotic ≥20% triggers bone-protective therapy (bisphosphonate or denosumab). Calcium, vit D, smoking cessation, weight-bearing exercise for all on ADT.

edits.match: Conventional imaging (CT abd/pelvis + Tc-99m bone scan)
edits.new: **nmCRPC imaging** (rising PSA, castrate testosterone, no metastases) — conventional or PSMA PET imaging every 6–12 months; may extend to annually once on ARPI without other progression indicators. PSA every 3–6 months with PSADT calculation.

edits.match: PSMA PET/CT — at BCR with negative or equivocal conventional imaging
edits.new: **PSMA PET/CT** — initial staging of unfavorable intermediate / high-risk disease: PSMA PET OR bone scan + cross-sectional imaging (AUA/ASTRO 2026, strong); PSMA PET may be added if conventional imaging is negative; not routine in asymptomatic low / favorable-intermediate risk. PSA recurrence after exhaustion of local therapy: PSMA PET preferred (greater sensitivity) or when conventional imaging is negative (AUA/SUO 2026). Periodic restaging in advanced disease.

edits.match: DRE on active surveillance — annually. No new nodularity
edits.new: **DRE on active surveillance** — annually (NCCN; AUA/ASTRO 2026 allows every 1–2 years — annual retained as more conservative). No new nodularity.

edits.match: USPSTF 2018 grade C (shared decision 55–69) and grade D
edits.new: **PSA screening framework disagreement.** USPSTF 2018 grade C (shared decision 55–69) and grade D (≥70) is more restrictive than AUA/SUO Early Detection (2023; amended 2026), which endorses baseline PSA at 45–50 and risk-stratified screening through age 70+ in healthy men. USPSTF update in progress (no draft posted as of Nov 2026).

edits.match: AUA 2023 update strongly supports PSMA PET for staging
edits.new: **PSMA PET utilization.** AUA/ASTRO 2026 makes PSMA PET an equal alternative to conventional imaging for staging unfavorable intermediate / high-risk disease; AUA/SUO 2026 makes it the preferred modality at PSA recurrence after local therapy. CMS coverage is broad for FDA-approved tracers, but local contractor policies vary.

**AS PSA interval and post-treatment PSA cadence.** NCCN uses PSA every 3–6 months on active surveillance; AUA/ASTRO 2026 advises no more often than every 6 months — flagged, NCCN cadence retained. After curative therapy, AUA/ASTRO 2026 (q3–6 mo × 2 yr, q6 mo yr 2–5) is more frequent than NCCN / ACS (q6–12 mo × 5 yr) — AUA cadence adopted.

PSA on active surveillance (q3–6 mo NCCN; AUA ≥q6 mo); PSA post-curative q3–6 mo first 2 yr (AUA); testosterone on ADT (q3–6 mo, target <50 ng/dL); PSA on ADT / AR-pathway inhibitor / nmCRPC; abiraterone LFTs / K+ / BP (q2 wk × 3 mo then monthly); mCRPC baseline labs (CBC, CMP, ALP, LDH, Hgb) each cycle
PSA post-curative (q6 mo years 2–5)
DEXA on ADT (baseline, at 1 yr, then every 1–2 yr); MRI prostate on AS (every 1–3 yr)

Confirmatory biopsy on AS within ~12 mo (MRI first if not MRI-guided), then every 1–4 yr or as triggered; germline testing (all advanced) + somatic (metastatic); PSMA PET/CT preferred at BCR, or PSMA PET vs CT + bone scan for unfavorable intermediate / high-risk staging; conventional CT abd/pelvis + Tc-99m bone scan at BCR / progression; imaging in nmCRPC q6–12 mo, mCRPC at least annually; eGFR / Cr per agent
DEXA on ADT (baseline, at 1 yr, then every 1–2 yr); mpMRI on AS (every 1–3 yr)

PSMA PET/CT preferred at BCR after local therapy; PSMA PET or CT + bone scan for unfavorable intermediate / high-risk staging; CT abd/pelvis + bone scan at progression; nmCRPC imaging q6–12 mo; mCRPC imaging at least annually (sooner if PSADT short or symptoms)
L: PSA on AS, PSA post-curative q3–6 mo yr 1–2, testosterone + PSA on ADT, abiraterone LFTs/K+/BP
L: PSA post-curative (q6 mo yr 2–5)
I: DEXA on ADT (baseline, 1 yr, then q1–2 yr); mpMRI on AS (q1–3 yr)
I: confirmatory biopsy on AS (≤12 mo then q1–4 yr); PSMA PET preferred at BCR; CT + bone scan at progression; nmCRPC imaging q6–12 mo; mCRPC ≥ annually · L: germline / somatic testing (advanced)

edits.match: Medication review with AGS Beers Criteria — every visit
edits.new: **Medication review with AGS Beers Criteria** — every visit (required element of CPT 99483). Avoid / deprescribe anticholinergics, benzodiazepines, Z-drugs, first-generation antihistamines; address cumulative anticholinergic burden. Use the AGS 2025 Beers Alternatives guidance for non-pharmacologic-first and safer pharmacologic substitutes; identify the underlying cause of the symptom and monitor for recurrence after withdrawal.

edits.match: USPSTF 2020 issued an I-statement (insufficient evidence) on screening asymptomatic community-dwelling adults ≥65
edits.new: USPSTF 2020 issued an I-statement (insufficient evidence) on screening asymptomatic community-dwelling adults ≥65 (update in progress; research plan finalized 2025, I-statement remains operative)

edits.match: AAN endorses one-time structural imaging at diagnosis; no guideline supports
edits.new: **Routine repeat neuroimaging.** AAN endorses one-time structural imaging at diagnosis; no guideline supports surveillance imaging absent clinical change. An AAN Etiologic Diagnosis of Dementia guideline is in draft (public comment); the 2001 parameter remains operative until it is finalized.

edits.match: ASCO/ACS (Runowicz 2016) and ASCO Follow-Up (Khatcheressian 2013), still the operative US framework and reinforced by NCCN Breast Cancer v5.2025, call for a detailed cancer-related history and physical exam every 3–6 months for the first 3 years, every 6–12 months years 4–5, then annually, plus annual mammography (ipsilateral breast after lumpectomy / radiation; contralateral only after mastectomy)
edits.new: ASCO 2026 (Nahleh) replaces the uniform 2013 follow-up schedule with risk-tiered surveillance: low intensity (DCIS; stage I HR+ off systemic therapy; TNBC / HER2+ ≥5 yr from diagnosis) — annual visit, in person or virtual, suitable for primary care / survivorship / APP / gynecology; intermediate (stage I TNBC / HER2+ <5 yr; stage II–III TNBC / HER2+ with pCR; on endocrine therapy) — H&P every 6–12 months for 5–10 years; high (TNBC / HER2+ with residual disease <5 yr; inflammatory BC <10 yr; germline BRCA1/2 / PALB2; HR+ on endocrine therapy + CDK4/6 inhibitor; active systemic therapy) — H&P every 3–6 months up to 10 years with chest-wall exam every 6 months. Mammography remains annual by default (NCCN / ACS); ASCO 2026 permits every 1–2 years after 3 recurrence-free years in low-risk breast-conservation patients ≥50 (conflict flagged). Runowicz 2016 remains the operative framework for late-effects and survivorship care

edits.match: Breast MRI is reserved for women meeting ACS high-risk criteria
edits.new: Breast MRI is offered by shared decision to germline carriers, women with chest radiation at age 10–30, and selected others (diagnosis <50, lobular histology, mammographically occult cancer, extremely dense breasts)

edits.match: Routine CBC, chemistries, LFTs, tumor markers, chest imaging, CT, bone scan, and PET are explicitly NOT recommended in asymptomatic survivors
edits.new: Routine CBC, chemistries, LFTs, tumor markers, ctDNA, chest imaging, CT, bone scan, and PET are explicitly NOT recommended in asymptomatic survivors

edits.match: Cancer-related history and physical examination — every 3–6 months for first 3 years
edits.new: **Cancer-related history and physical examination** — risk-tiered (ASCO 2026): low intensity annually (in person or virtual); intermediate every 6–12 months for 5–10 years; high every 3–6 months up to 10 years, chest-wall exam every 6 months.

edits.match: Mammography of intact breast — annually post-mastectomy
edits.new: **Mammography** — annually (default; NCCN / ACS). After breast-conserving surgery: annual; ASCO 2026 permits every 1–2 years after 3 recurrence-free years if age ≥50 with low-risk features (T1, low grade, node-negative, ER+) by shared decision; age <50 or TNBC / HER2+ remain annual. After unilateral mastectomy: annual contralateral. After bilateral mastectomy: not recommended unless symptomatic.

edits.match: Breast MRI — annually as adjunct to mammography only if ACS high-risk criteria
edits.new: **Supplemental breast MRI** — offer via shared decision for germline carriers (BRCA1/2, PTEN, STK11, TP53, etc.) with intact breast tissue and for chest radiation at age 10–30; consider when diagnosed <50, invasive lobular histology, cancer missed by / within 12 months of a negative mammogram, or extremely dense breasts. Contrast-enhanced mammography or US if MRI unavailable / contraindicated. No evidence MRI surveillance improves survival.

edits.match: Calcium / vitamin D adequacy — ongoing counseling during AI therapy
edits.new: **Circulating tumor DNA (ctDNA / cfDNA)** — NOT recommended for recurrence monitoring outside a clinical trial or research setting.

edits.match: ASCO / NCCN / ACS strongly recommend AGAINST routine CT
edits.new: ASCO 2026 / NCCN / ACS strongly recommend AGAINST routine CT

edits.match: USPSTF 2024 mammography (Grade B, biennial 40–74)
edits.new: **Mammography interval conflict.** ASCO 2026 permits every 1–2-year mammography after 3 recurrence-free years in low-risk breast-conservation patients ≥50 (Mammo-50); NCCN / ACS retain annual. Default annual; de-escalate by shared decision.
Routine CBC, chemistry, LFTs, tumor markers (CEA, CA 15-3, CA 27.29), and ctDNA NOT recommended for asymptomatic stage I-III survivors
Mammography of intact / ipsilateral breast (annual default; q1–2 yr option after 3 recurrence-free yr in low-risk post-BCS age ≥50 per ASCO 2026)

Supplemental breast MRI by shared decision (germline carriers, chest radiation age 10–30; consider age <50 at diagnosis, lobular, occult cancer, extremely dense breasts); routine surveillance CT / bone scan / PET NOT recommended in asymptomatic stage I-III survivors
Cancer-related H&P every 3–6 months (high-intensity tier, up to 10 yr); chest-wall exam every 6 months (high tier)
Cancer-related H&P every 6–12 months (intermediate tier, 5–10 yr) or annually (low tier); annual gynecologic assessment (tamoxifen — evaluate AUB promptly, no routine TVUS / biopsy)
P: H&P q3–6 mo (high-intensity tier); I: echo q6 mo × 2 yr post-trastuzumab

I: annual mammography (q1–2 yr option, low-risk ≥50 after 3 yr) · P: H&P q6–12 mo (intermediate) / annual (low tier); annual gyn (tamoxifen) · L: lipid + Ca/vit D (AI) · S: lifestyle, second-primary screening
I: breast MRI by shared decision (germline / chest RT / selected); routine surveillance CT / bone / PET / markers / ctDNA NOT recommended

edits.new: GINA 2026 recommends against SABA-only reliever therapy

edits.match: Biologic candidacy assessment — when severe / uncontrolled despite high-dose ICS-LABA
edits.new: **Biologic candidacy assessment** — when severe / uncontrolled despite high-dose ICS-LABA and confirmed adherence / technique. Mepolizumab, benralizumab, reslizumab, depemokimab (anti-IL-5, SC every 6 months; FDA Dec 2025, age ≥12, eosinophilic phenotype), dupilumab, omalizumab, tezepelumab.

edits.match: Vaccination status — annually. Influenza, COVID-19 per CDC
edits.new: **Vaccination status** — annually. Influenza annually (≥65: HD-IIV3, RIV3, or aIIV3 preferred); COVID-19 per current-season CDC guidance (2026–27: recommended for all adults ≥18; ≥65 two doses ~6 months apart); pneumococcal at age ≥50: one dose PCV20 or PCV21, or PCV15 followed by PPSV23 ≥1 year later; RSV single dose at ≥75 or at 50–74 with chronic lung disease (asthma qualifies; self-attestation acceptable); Tdap / Td per schedule.

edits.match: Annual influenza, COVID-19, and pneumococcal vaccinations are standard
edits.new: Annual influenza and current-season COVID-19 vaccination are standard, with one-time pneumococcal vaccination at ≥50 and RSV at ≥75 (or 50–74 with asthma)

Comorbidity surveillance (allergic rhinitis / CRS, GERD, obesity / BMI, OSA screen, VCD / ILO, anxiety / depression); vaccination status (influenza annually, COVID-19 per current CDC season guidance, PCV20 / PCV21 or PCV15 → PPSV23 at ≥50, RSV ×1 at ≥75 or 50–74 with asthma, Tdap)
